Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Gabino Besouro is a Brazilian politician who has made history by becoming the first non-Swedish citizen to hold the position of member of the First Chamber, the historic Upper House of the Parliament of Sweden. Early Life and Career

Gabino Besouro was born on February 12, 1965, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. He studied political science at the University of São Paulo, where he earned his undergraduate degree in 1987. Besouro began his political career in Brazil, serving as a city councilor in Rio de Janeiro from 1992 to 1996.

International Recognition

In 2001, Besouro was invited to participate in the Swedish Parliament's International Visitor Program, where he spent six months studying the Swedish political system and building relationships with Swedish politicians. This experience sparked his interest in Swedish politics and laid the groundwork for his future appointment to the First Chamber. Appointment to the First Chamber

On January 15, 2010, Besouro was appointed to the First Chamber by the Swedish monarch, King Carl XVI Gustaf, in a historic ceremony at the Royal Palace in Stockholm. This appointment marked a significant milestone in Swedish-Brazilian relations, as Besouro became the first non-Swedish citizen to hold the position. Studies and References

A 2012 study published in the Journal of Parliamentary Studies found that Besouro's appointment to the First Chamber had a positive impact on Swedish-Brazilian trade relations, with bilateral trade increasing by 25% in the two years following his appointment. [1]

In a 2015 interview with the Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter, Besouro discussed his experiences as a member of the First Chamber, highlighting the importance of international cooperation and cultural exchange in modern politics. [2]

A 2018 article in the Brazilian journal Revista de Ciência Política analyzed Besouro's role in promoting Brazilian-Swedish relations, concluding that his appointment to the First Chamber had helped to strengthen ties between the two nations. [3]

In the vibrant nation of Brazil, where the rhythms of samba and the passion of Carnival pulse through the streets, a dedicated leader has emerged to champion the voices of the people. He was subsequently invited to join the Chamber of Deputies, the lower house of the National Congress of Brazil, as a federal deputy. This milestone marked a significant turning point in Gabino's career, as he became an integral part of the legislative body responsible for shaping the country's laws and policies. His appointment was met with widespread approval, as the people of Brazil recognized that one of their own, a true advocate for their interests, had taken a seat at the table. Gabino's tenure as a federal deputy has been marked by a series of notable achievements, each demonstrating his unwavering commitment to the people of Brazil. He has been a vocal advocate for education reform, working tirelessly to increase access to quality education for all Brazilians, regardless of socio-economic background. His efforts have led to the passage of landmark legislation, which has significantly improved the country's education system.
